questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but the shared apartment I stayed in was quite expensive. Next time, I would book an airbnb for one month and then search for a place to stay, while I'm already there, since it's way easier to find a cheap place then

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sillim is the closest neighbourhood to SNU and while it has a bad reputation, I really liked it. I always felt safe and while it is a quieter area, there still are nice (cheap) coffee shops and restaurants. Other areas I'd recommend are somewhere near snu station or Sadang. From all these areas you have free shuttle buses going to SNU

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: no

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I received a rejection at first, without any explanation and had then to apply to another institute. When I talked to other exchange students, a lot of them experienced the same, but some of their home university were more insistent on asking snu why there was a rejection and without any explanation, they then got an acceptance for the institute they originally applied for without having to apply again.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to hand in a cv and a motivation letter. I remember it was extremely difficult to decide for which specific institute to apply for, because while the content of all courses offered was translated into english, it was completely unclear, which of them were actually held in English and not in Korean. Because of that, at first I applied for the International Relation institute, for which I later found out, that they only offered one course in English this semester. I was rejected from that institute without any explanation (they also wrote directly to me and not the international office of KU), applied for the Graduate school for public administration and was accepted. After being accepted SNU provides a lot of information about how to apply for a visa etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: FAQ, an exchange student guide etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: it was really stressful, because it happens on a first come first serve basis and courses are full within seconds. Additionally, registration period starts due to the time difference at 1am. Nonetheless, I almost got into all the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: start to register as soon as it's possible. Otherwise, you will not get into the courses you want to get into. There is also a drop period, so you can sign up for more courses than you actually need, try all of them out and then drop the ones you liked the least.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: interesting due to the different perspective, but we never received any feedback from the professors

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'd say courses were generally easier. However, it seems like it very much depends on the professor. Some of the other exchange students (in the same major) had an insane amount of workload to handle, while others almost had to do nothing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In most of the courses, teaching is less interactive

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding International Security
Theories of Global Public Policy and Institutions
Political Economy of Economic Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just go for what sounds interesting to you. Like I said I'd recommend to register for more courses than you actually need and then just attend the first few lectures, see if the course is about what you expected it to be about and drop the ones you dislike

questions.answer: the hierarchical difference between professor and students

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the kindness of koreans

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't book a course at the LEI. Instead, attend the free language course SNU offers. If you are vegan of vegetarian, it will be extremly difficult for you to find food in Korea. You absolutely need a Korean phone number and if possible a korean bank card. A lot of things are just possible if you have one or even both of these things.
